text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Publisher VNU in talks with CLT-UFA about sale of its minority stake in Belgian commercial TV station VTM. (p1)
- Informal capital market -- where wealthy entrepreneurs put money into young start-up firms -- running at around Dfl 3.5 billion - economic affairs ministry research. (p1)
- Paper and packaging group KNPBT and Dutch PTT (KPN) to reach amicable agreement on their similar names. (p1)
- Italian Pirelli group to make public bid for all outstanding shares and warrants of Pirelli Tyre Holding (PTH) on the Amsterdam bourse. (p1)
- Office supplier Ahrend posts 25 pct profit growth in 1996 on nine percent turnover rise. (p3)
- Confectioner Klene seeks 1-for-10 share split. (p3)
- Printer Plantijn takes over Rotterdam-based Rozet. (p3)
- Construction production to rise three percent in 1997, says building trade's economic analysis organisation EIB. (p4)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Dutch couturier Frank Govers (64) dies. (p1)
- Philips Electronics seeks to sell loss-making video chain Super Club; Free Record Shop says not interested. (p2)
- Economic Affairs Minister Hans Wijers grants subsidy to copier firm Oce van der Grinten for research into new inkjet technologies. (p2)
- U.N. children fund Unicef supports critics of baby food maker Nutricia. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Soccer association (KNVB) reckons to get Dfl 250 million for a new 2.5 year TV broadcasting licence. (p1)
- Share prices of smaller companies on Midkap-index rise faster than those on main AEX-index. (p19)
- Film and music group Polygram, 75 pct Philips-owned, buys rival EMI chief. (p21)
- Dutch mid-sized businesses optimistic about 1997. (p21)
TROUW
- Foreign Affairs Minister does not exclude supplying Turkey with air defence missiles. (p5)
- Future of APN, the first postal firm to rival Dutch PTT Post, hangs by a thread. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- ABN AMRO estimates rival ING's hidden reserves at 2.8 billion guilders. (p10)
- Philips Asia chief, Frans Sluiter, resigns unexpectedly. (p11)
